research_result.description: Discord is a communications platform offering messaging, voice, real-time events, and interactive features accessible via REST APIs, Gateway WebSockets, and developer applications.
research_result.credential_requirements: Developers can create applications and obtain bot tokens or OAuth2 credentials for free via the self-serve Discord Developer Portal. Certain privileged intents or partner scopes require app verification or explicit approval.

evidence.claim: Discord provides a REST API to access and manipulate platform resources.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The Discord API is a REST API that allows you to interact with Discord data from your own applications.

evidence.claim: Discord supports OAuth2 authorization and standard OAuth2 flows.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: OAuth2 enables application developers to build applications that utilize authentication and data from the Discord API.

evidence.claim: Calls to OAuth2 endpoints support HTTP Basic authentication.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: All calls to the OAuth2 endpoints require either HTTP Basic authentication or client_id and client_secret supplied in the form data body.

evidence.claim: Discord API requests can be authenticated using bot tokens.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Using a bot token found on the Bot page within your app's settings.

evidence.claim: Discord API requests can be authenticated using OAuth2 bearer tokens.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Using an OAuth2 bearer token gained through the OAuth2 API.

evidence.claim: Developers can create applications self-serve in the developer portal.
